1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the material
brought on record.

2. This bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in Case Crime No.30 of 2024, under
Sections - 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Padri, District-
Mirzapur with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.

sentences.text: 3.  It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is father-in-law of deceased.

The marriage of deceased with son of applicant has taken place about nine months prior to the incident but the allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased levelled against the applicant are wholly false.

sentences.text:
allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused,
including the applicant.

Learned counsel has referred the statements of several independent witnesses, including that of Arjun Yadav and Chandu Pasi, who have inter alia stated that they have never heard about any dowry demand or any other complaint.
It was submitted that deceased has committed suicide by consuming poison due to minor dispute with her husband.
After incident, she was taken to the hospital but she could not survive.
In postmortem report, no injury has been shown on body of deceased and cause of death could not be ascertained, hence, viscera was preserved.
Viscera report is yet be received.
It is further submitted that applicant was living separately from deceased and her husband and in this connection documents have been attached as annexure no.3.

Lastly, it was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 21.03.2024, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that deceased has suffered unnatural death other than under normal circumstances within a short period of her marriage.
5. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
6.
The bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant - Raj Kumar Yadav involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate any of the prosecution witness.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
8. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
